shapes.name: runtime_safety_off_and_977_reduction
shapes.reason: fe_mul median stayed 14 ns. ReleaseSafe fe_mul is 604 bytes with 24 mul and 22 umulh and no library call; the reduction is three widening multiplies by 0x1000003d1, not a loop. @setRuntimeSafety(false) left that object the same size, because the widening product cannot overflow. A straight-line multiply by 977 plus a 32-bit shift was correct against the division test and was 372 bytes with 16 mul and 16 umulh in isolation, but in the node bench fe_inv moved 740 to 1253 ns, point_double 89 to 112 ns, and ecdsa_verify 37202 to 40910 ns. Reverted.

shapes.name: glv_endomorphism
shapes.reason: Both scalars are already split. The package test derives beta and lambda as cube roots, checks lambda^3 = 1 mod n, beta^3 = 1 mod p, and beta*G = lambda*G, and checks the reduced basis. The joint chain has four terms. ECDSA doublings are 127. A second endomorphism pass would not shorten that chain.

residual: fe_mul is 14 ns and 1950 operations, 96 percent of the October 4 ECDSA verify and still the gap after shapes 0-3. The widening u256 multiply is already 24 mul and 22 umulh with no library call. Safety-off and a 977-and-shift reduction left the median at 14 ns and slowed verify, so they were reverted. The count is already the four-term GLV joint schedule: width-16 G, width-4 P, 127 doublings. Window 5 moved the ECDSA count by 1.9 percent and was reverted. The uncommitted lazy 5x52 measured 72 ns. The committed 5x52 kernel in Project/scripts/zig_crypto_open/field52.zig returns Field(1) from mul, so every product runs the carry and the 2^256 fold before the next addition, and the value is a five-limb struct passed by value. That is a reduction on every operation plus a memory round trip. A lazy field only beats the register u256 multiply if the five limbs stay unnormalized across double and mixed and are normalized at compares. That representation was not retried. A dedicated 4x64 square, 10 limb multiplies against 16, lowered the isolated fe_sqr own min from 13.15 ns to 11.93 ns and left the verify field-op total at 1950, of which 808 were squares. Point.double called that square five times (bl _root.sqr) and the square spilled a 0xc0 frame, so point_double moved from 88.10 ns to 94.63 ns and the verify ratio_min values rose. Reverted. A lazy 5x52 field with one 2^260 fold and no normalize inside mul raised fe_mul from 12.38 ns to 34.79 ns. point_double contains 71 str and 39 ldr, against 10 str and 9 ldr for the inlined widening multiply, and it calls fe_mul, which opens with sub sp, #0x110. ECDSA normalizes 73 times. Reverted. ReleaseFast codegen, with runtime safety turned off because an imported module still emitted overflow checks, shrank point_double from sub sp, #0xe0 (10 str, 9 ldr, two panic bls) to sub sp, #0xc0 (9 str, 7 ldr, no bl). fe_mul is still the inlined widening multiply: 24 mul and 22 umulh, and no sub sp of its own. A bench at load 12.7 read ECDSA ratio_min 1.667 against 1.920 while fe_mul read 27.54 ns against 12.38 ns, so that ratio is not a keep. Forcing inline on mul, add, sub, reduceField, and times left point_double with no field bl, sub sp, #0xc0, 8 str and 6 ldr. ECDSA ratio_min was 1.872 against 1.920.
